cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: GAIL has proposed a ₹123.42-crore plant at the KCDC site to process 300 tonnes of Bengaluru’s segregated organic waste daily into compressed biogas and manure.

lead.headline: PINK LINE TO OPEN ON NOVEMBER 14, TAKING BENGALURU METRO PAST 100 KM
lead.deck: The 7.5-km elevated Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch is set to begin passenger service at 6 a.m., adding a key Bannerghatta Road connection.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the elevated Pink Line section on November 14. Passenger services on the 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere corridor are set to start at 6 a.m.

The opening will take Bengaluru’s operational metro network beyond 100 km for the first time, to about 103 km. The line includes the Jayadeva interchange, connecting Bannerghatta Road commuters to the wider network.
The Economic Times reports that the new stretch will link passengers with destinations including Electronic City, Silk Board, HSR Layout, Jayanagar, Majestic and Whitefield.

sidebarStory.headline: CABINET SETS ₹62,370-CRORE RABI FERTILISER SUBSIDY
sidebarStory.subhead: The allocation is 64% higher than last year; DAP will continue at a fixed price of ₹1,350 per bag.
paragraphs: The Union Cabinet approved ₹62,370 crore in subsidy for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for the 2026–27 rabi season, a 64% increase over last year’s allocation.
The subsidy applies from October 1 to March 31. The government said its special provision to keep a 50-kg bag of di-ammonium phosphate at ₹1,350 will continue.

stories.headline: AI PILOT HELPS CITY POLICE REACH 1.5 LAKH 112 CALLERS
paragraphs: Bengaluru police say a three-month pilot using multilingual AI calls gathered feedback from more than 1.5 lakh people who used the 112 emergency response service.
Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said average response time had fallen from about 15 minutes to six minutes. Trained staff will continue to handle sensitive and complex conversations.

stories.headline: POLICE RECOVER OLYMPIC GOLD AND SEVEN OTHER MEDALS STOLEN FROM MM SOMAYA
paragraphs: Police arrested two people and recovered the 1980 Olympic gold medal and seven other international medals belonging to former India hockey captain M.M. Somaya.
A Kodava dagger, camera, Olympic kit bag and the two-wheeler allegedly used in the theft were also recovered, police said.

stories.headline: MASTER PLAN SOUGHT FOR TIN FACTORY JUNCTION BOTTLENECK
paragraphs: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has directed the city authority and metro agencies to prepare an integrated plan for the congested KR Puram junction.
The proposal is to coordinate bus bays, metro and bus transfers, taxi access and pedestrian safety; officials were also told to restore roads affected by construction.

groups.ariaLabel: India public affairs, security and policy news

stories.headline: THREE CRPF PERSONNEL INJURED IN KULGAM CHECKPOINT ATTACK
paragraphs: Suspected terrorists opened fire on a CRPF checkpoint in Kulgam district on Wednesday, injuring three personnel; one was reported to be critical.
Security forces launched a search operation. The Indian Express reported that investigators were questioning three suspected overground workers over possible logistical support.

image.caption: Security personnel in Kulgam after Wednesday’s attack. Photo: ANI / The Indian Express

stories.headline: INDIA STREAMLINES VISA SYSTEM, CUTS MAIN CATEGORIES FROM 13 TO 9
paragraphs: The Home Ministry has reduced India’s main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23. It says application forms will ask for 65–70% fewer fields.
The revised framework widens the visitor visa to cover some short business, medical and cultural visits. Visas under the new system are expected to begin by the end of 2026.

stories.headline: CABINET CLEARS ₹3,230-CRORE YUGE YUGEEN BHARAT MUSEUM
paragraphs: The Union Cabinet approved a ₹3,230-crore project to develop the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in the North and South Block complex in New Delhi.
The plan will adapt the historic buildings into a museum tracing India’s civilisational history, with completion targeted for 2031.

stories.headline: FOUR CHAURI CHAURA EXPRESS COACHES DERAIL IN UTTAR PRADESH
paragraphs: Four coaches of the Chauri Chaura Express derailed while leaving Kanpur Central on Wednesday evening. No passengers were injured or killed, North Central Railway said.
The Railways arranged a special train for affected passengers and offered full refunds to those who did not wish to continue their journey.

stories.headline: DEADLINE TO CLEAR LEGACY LANDFILLS EXTENDED TO DECEMBER 2027
paragraphs: The Centre has pushed back the deadline to remediate legacy dumpsites across the country to December 2027.
The work falls under Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0, launched in 2021; the original mission period was due to end on October 1, 2026.

stories.headline: NAVI MUMBAI TOPS INDIA’S CLEANEST-CITY SURVEY
paragraphs: Navi Mumbai was named India’s cleanest city in the 2025–26 Swachh Survekshan, the Centre’s tenth annual cleanliness survey.
Surat and Vijayawada placed second and third, respectively.

stories.headline: ₹250-CRORE FUNDING FOR PROPOSED AGROWASTE-TO-FUELS PLANT
paragraphs: Greenjoules has secured ₹250 crore for a proposed plant that would convert agricultural residues such as paddy straw, husk and bagasse into bio-crude.
The company says its process uses catalytic treatment to turn farm waste into fuel, creating another possible use for crop residues.

stories.headline: MAINLY CLEAR TODAY; NO CITY WARNING IN FORCE

paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department forecasts mainly clear skies for Bengaluru on Thursday, with a minimum of 19°C and maximum of 29°C. No warning is in force.
